articles.title: How Tom Brady’s 7 Super Bowl rings and 13-year marriage to Gisele Bündchen reveal the cost of chasing greatness
articles.summary: Tom Brady retired with seven Super Bowl rings, but his marriage to Gisele Bündchen ended before he left the game for good.
articles.body: Tom Brady retired with seven Super Bowl rings, but his marriage to Gisele Bündchen ended before he left the game for good. The couple announced their divorce on October 28, 2022, closing a 13-year marriage. It came only months after Brady retired in February 2022 and then reversed that decision 40 days later. He was beginning his 23rd season. Bündchen had said openly that she worried about the toll football was taking on him and their family. Brady's titles are a league record, and the divorce shows what it cost to keep adding to it.Tom Brady's seven Super Bowl rings came with a heavy cost at homeSix of the rings came in New England and one in Tampa Bay. The last arrived in February 2021, when Brady was 43. He and Bündchen had married in 2009, when he already had three titles, so almost the whole run of his late career happened inside the marriage.Late careers are not free. They are built on strict routines.Brady's diet, sleep schedule and training plan were famously rigid, and a house with three children does not bend easily around that kind of discipline. He has a son, Jack, from an earlier relationship. He and Bündchen have two children together, Benjamin and Vivian. Someone had to carry the daily load while he chased one more season, and in most years that was Bündchen, who had her own career to manage.The breaking point looked sudden from outside, but the signs were there. Brady stepped away in February 2022, and by mid-March he announced he was coming back. In August he left Buccaneers training camp for 11 days, and the team called it a personal matter. Bündchen said in interviews that she hoped he would eventually put football second and that she had needs of her own. Brady's choice to keep playing was a choice about her time as well as his.What the split says about elite sport and family lifeThe easy reading is that football beat the marriage. That is too neat. Plenty of athletes keep both, and nobody outside the home can know what went wrong there. Both of them described the divorce as a decision made with care and said they remained committed to raising their children together.Still, Brady's case stands out because the chase had no natural end. Most players leave when their bodies stop answering. Brady's body kept answering, so the decision never got made for him. He had to make it himself, and he made it late.That is the real lesson for fans who treat longevity as pure virtue. Playing until 45 is a feat, but it also asks everyone nearby to put their lives on hold. A family can absorb that for a few years. Fifteen is a lot harder.Brady has since moved into broadcasting with Fox and a minority stake in the Las Vegas Raiders, jobs that keep him in the sport without the weekly grind of playing. It is a calmer schedule than the one he kept for two decades, and it arrived after the marriage was over, not before.Seven rings will be hard for anyone to match. articles.title: Travis Kelce-backed $200 million Six Flags faces fresh scrutiny after metal bracket falls from roller coaster amid growing ride safety concerns
articles.summary: Six Flags is facing renewed questions about ride safety after a metal bracket fell from a roller coaster at Cedar Point in Ohio.
articles.body: Six Flags is facing renewed questions about ride safety after a metal bracket fell from a roller coaster at Cedar Point in Ohio. The incident ended without injuries, but its timing has drawn attention following a fatal accident at another park in the chain. The developments also bring NFL star Travis Kelce into the wider conversation, given his reported ties to Six Flags as an ambassador and investor. While there is no indication that Kelce had any involvement in the incidents, the latest scare puts the amusement park company's safety practices under fresh public scrutiny.Six Flags roller coaster incident prompts fresh safety concernsCedar Point temporarily shut down its Millennium Force roller coaster on Friday, October 16, after a small metal bracket reportedly came loose from one of its ride vehicles and landed in an area used by park guests.Fortunately, nobody was struck by the falling component, and the park reported no injuries. Officials took the ride out of service while they reviewed the incident and carried out the necessary inspections.Millennium Force returned to operation on Saturday evening after completing maintenance inspections and safety checks. A Cedar Point spokesperson confirmed the reopening in a statement to local media."The ride has resumed operations following the successful completion of maintenance inspections and all required safety checks."The spokesperson also stressed the park's commitment to protecting visitors and employees. However, publicly available reports have not established why the bracket became detached.The incident comes at a difficult time for Six Flags. On October 12, 42-year-old Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem died after falling from the Goliath roller coaster at Six Flags Over Georgia. Authorities are investigating the circumstances surrounding his death.Following that tragedy, several similar roller coasters across the company's parks were temporarily taken out of service for precautionary safety reviews. The separate incidents have increased attention on the company's attractions and the importance of effective inspection procedures.Travis Kelce's Six Flags ties draw attention amid ride safety concernsTravis Kelce's reported involvement with Six Flags as an ambassador and investor adds another layer of public interest to the developing story.The Kansas City Chiefs tight end has built a profile that extends well beyond football, with business interests and commercial partnerships adding to his public presence. His connection to the amusement park company means developments involving its operations may attract attention from both NFL fans and the wider public.Still, Kelce's business association should not be confused with responsibility for individual ride operations. There is no evidence linking him personally to either roller coaster incident, and maintenance decisions remain matters for the company's operating teams and relevant safety authorities.For Six Flags, the immediate priority is ensuring that its attractions meet required safety standards and that investigations into reported incidents receive proper attention.Although Millennium Force has reopened, questions about the cause of the detached bracket remain unanswered in public reports. articles.title: It’s been ugly, but the Broncos survived brutal 6-game stretch with 4-2 record
articles.summary: The Denver Broncos' remaining schedule, on paper, is much easier than their first six games.
articles.body:
It was a long, hard road through the first six weeks of the 2026 NFL season for the Denver Broncos , but they emerged from the difficult stretch with a 4-2 record, and well in the thick of the AFC playoff picture .

In Weeks 1-6, the Broncos faced nearly the entire NFC West, including the 2025 Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks , 2026 Super Bowl favorites in the Los Angeles Rams and the San Francisco 49ers , and the Kansas City Chiefs. After a Week 1 blowout loss to Kansas City in Arrowhead, the Broncos bounced back with wins over the Jacksonville Jaguars and Rams, before a loss to the San Francisco 49ers, followed by a win over the hapless Los Angeles Chargers, and finally a win over Seattle last week.

"It's a great test, it's right where we wanted to be," offensive lineman Mike McGlinchey said of opponents faced over the first six weeks. "You don't want to come into this league and pray for easy wins. This is the NFL, it's the greatest league in the world. There's so many teams worthy of being successful, but at the end of the day you have to execute when you're on the football field. We've been finding enough ways to do that to get four wins on the board against really, really great teams, and certainly some great defenses. I'm excited for where we're headed."

The Broncos haven't come out of this stretch unscathed: their secondary of Talanoa Hufanga, Pat Surtain and Riley Moss have all missed time, rookie running back Jonah Coleman was placed on IR after a hard-fought performance (he is eligible to possibly return this week), and quarterback Bo Nix has played some of the worst football of his young career to date.

Nix spoke on the offensive struggles from his perspective, explaining that a lot of the struggles have come because of the opponents they've faced.

"I do think you have to [attribute it to] the schedule, just the first six games we knew were going to be tough," Nix said. "To come out 4-2 with really a complete team effort in all six games, it's a complete team effort to get four of those wins. We came up short just barely in San Fran. We could be 5-1. 4-2 is a really good spot, and then as an offense, we'll figure out ways to continue to improve."

Other players like running back J.K. Dobbins just care that the Broncos are winning.

Coach Sean Payton knows that the Broncos' record could just as easily be much worse, especially since Denver has had to come from behind in three of their four wins to start the season. But what about the team's start gives him reason to smile?

"The record," Payton deadpanned to reporters on Thursday. "Meaning I say that the record, because those wins are hard to get. So we just played a real good team, and I feel like we can continue to improve. Being at 4-2 right at this little three-day stretch and then get ready next week, that'd be the honest... And again, I'm a little bit of a realist to know that four and two could easily be two and four."

Quarterback Bo Nix had a similar takeaway.

"I do think there are some ways that we obviously will continue to improve," Nix said. "At the end of the day, the win is the most important."

The Broncos certainly hope to keep the momentum rolling into Week 7 when they go on the road to face the Arizona Cardinals.

articles.title: Former All-Pro WR Steve Smith points out glaring flaw in Rams' offense
articles.summary: Steve Smith called the Rams' offense "slow" and "unexplosive," which is leading to inconsistency and a lack of big plays.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams have sputtered out of the gate to begin their 2026 NFL season, going 2-4 through six games. There are many reasons behind their inability to secure wins, with media heads and analysts constantly throwing around ideas and theories.

Former NFL All-Pro receiver Steve Smith, who once predicted the success of Cooper Kupp despite massive pushback, issued his theory behind the team's struggles. On ESPN's "Get Up ," Smith claimed a lack of speed is hindering the offense.

"I use the word 'slow,'" stated Smith. "They are one mile per hour slower this year, and that has to do with they're sitting there in this 13 personnel, 13 personnel with three [tight ends]. They're going inside having Puka because he's another big body. That's four guys. None of these guys are beating anybody in the track meet, and so they're hiding the fact that they lack the speed and the vertical push to dictate to this offense, which makes them unexplosive on a consistent basis. You can't always use schemes to facilitate making big plays. Sometimes you got to allow some athletic guys to go up there and dictate to the defense."

While the Rams have kept their fastest receivers, Tutu Atwell and CJ Daniels, on the sideline, the offensive woes aren't coming from a lack of speed. Sure, the Rams would love to take the top off more, but it's their short-yardage attack that is dooming their offensive operation.

Matthew Stafford leads the NFL in passing yards. Perhaps having more speed would make teams more hesitant to blitz the Rams as much as they do. Regardless, Smith highlights a massive point.

The Rams often don't let their best playmakers dictate the defense, and ball distribution stifles the overall effort with a habitual bombardment of Nacua.

articles.title: Former Panthers captain suspended by NFL for spitting at opposing player
articles.summary: A former Panther has just become the second Bills safety this week to be suspended for spitting at an opponent.
articles.body:
This post has been updated with new information.

Whatever's in the water up in Carolina North must not taste very good.

The NFL has announced that they have issued a one-game suspension to Buffalo Bills safety Sam Franklin Jr. for spitting at an opponent during this past Sunday's game against the Las Vegas Raiders. Franklin, who began his pro career with the Carolina Panthers , is now the second Bills defender to be suspended this week for spitting at an opposing player—joining teammate C.J. Gardner-Johnson.

The Panthers signed Franklin as an undrafted free agent out of the University of Temple in 2020. He'd go on to become a special teams ace over his five-year tenure in Carolina, and was voted a team captain for his final campaign there in 2024.

Franklin appeared in a total of 74 games as a member of the Panthers—recording 105 combined tackles, a sack, an interception and a forced fumble.

He'd join the Bills in 2025, playing in all 19 of the team's outings. Buffalo then re-signed Franklin to a three-year deal in February.

According to league insider Tom Pelissero, Franklin denies the incident and will appeal his suspension.

articles.title: ‘Let Russ Cook,’ ‘No Reason For The Jets To Do This’ — Russell Wilson Pushes Chiefs To Swing Blockbuster Trade, But Fans Have a Few Things to Say
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs boast an undefeated 5-0 record so far this season. With expectations that the team could make another serious run at the Super Bowl, s...
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs boast an undefeated 5-0 record so far this season. With expectations that the team could make another serious run at the Super Bowl, speculation is increasing over whether the front office will make a major move to strengthen its roster.

Former NFL quarterback Russell Wilson has a specific target in mind, suggesting that Kansas City should pursue one of the New York Jets' wide receivers. His take sparked debate over both the potential benefits for Kansas City and the likelihood that New York would agree to such a deal.

Russell Wilson's Chiefs-Jets Trade Proposal Sparks Debate

The November 10 trade deadline is drawing closer, and the NFL fans are waiting to witness some blockbuster trades.

While sitting down with Kyle Long on "NFL on CBS," Russell proposed a surprising trade, which involved the Jets sending wide receiver Garrett Wilson to the Chiefs. While trading Garrett might seem unlikely, Russell made a case for the move.

"If I'm the Kansas City Chiefs, I got the All-Star running back in the backfield in Kenneth Walker, which we've never had before," Russell said . "And guess what that does? That play action opens up. What (Patrick) Mahomes does arguably better than anybody in the world is throw the ball down the field.

"If I'm thinking about this, who would I go get? I'm gonna go get Garrett Wilson. If the Jets keep losing, I'm gonna go get Garrett Wilson from the New York Jets because I believe that Garrett Wilson, down the field, with his ability- he's a smart guy; he learns quickly- he'd be great in the Andy Reid style of offense."

Russell also pointed out that the Chiefs have not had a receiver with Garrett's skill set.

PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN's Free NFL Playoff Predictor

Many from the NFL community supported Russell's proposal.

"Let Russ cook," former NFL quarterback Chase Daniel said .

"Would," Brad Henson Production, who covers the Chiefs, wrote on X.

"Won't ever happen, but this is THE move; it's not a 'swing' cause you know the level GW (Wilson) is at currently and can ascend to," one fan said. "Eliminates day 1 WR from the draft plans (and/or a big money FA) I'd call and at least gauge the market on him cause despite the early szn success we know what the Jets are and so do they."

Garrett had a relatively quiet outing in the Jets' loss to the New England Patriots on Sunday, recording four receptions on six targets for 44 yards.

BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN's Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator

However, since entering the NFL, Garrett has established himself as New York's primary receiving option. He currently holds an 82.8 grade in the PFN WR Impact Rankings , placing him at No. 12.

Garrett's role has led some fans to question why New York would consider trading away its top receiver.

"There is no reason for the Jets to do this. Like none. It'd have to be because Wilson wants out, and he just signed an extension there. Sauce (Gardner) was one thing, but having a true #1 WR for whatever QB you draft is way more important than an elite CB," another fan said .

"I mean this isn't realistic at all but would be easily bust open the window for the second part of our dynasty if it did happen," a fan added.

One more fan rejected the idea, writing, "Jets aren't trading him; they already have a lot of draft capital."

Garrett's contract situation also complicates the proposed move, as he agreed to a four-year, $130 million extension with New York last year. The deal made NFL history at the time, as he became the first receiver to secure an average annual salary exceeding $31 million after just three seasons in the league, which proved his worth to the team.

Unless New York receives an offer it considers worthwhile or Garrett expresses a desire to leave, Kansas City's pursuit of him will remain a speculative possibility rather than an upcoming move.

articles.title: NFL suspends Bills DB Sam Franklin Jr. 1 game for spitting at a Raiders player
articles.summary: Franklin is the second Bills player to be suspended for spitting at a Raiders player this week.
articles.body:
The NFL has suspended Buffalo Bills defensive back Sam Franklin Jr. for one game without pay for allegedly spitting at a player during Sunday's 33-30 win over the Las Vegas Raiders .

According to the NFL, the incident occurred with 1:32 left in the fourth quarter after the Raiders' extra point attempt.

Franklin denies the incident ever happened and is planning to appeal, according to WGR550's Sal Capaccio .

The suspension, if upheld, will cause Franklin to miss the Bills' Week 8 game against the Baltimore Ravens. Buffalo is on their bye week in Week 7. He will be eligible to return for the team's Monday night game against the Minnesota Vikings on Nov. 9.

Franklin is the second Bills player this week to be suspended for a spitting incident against the Raiders. The league announced Monday that C.J. Gardner-Johnson will miss a game after spitting on the ground toward the feet of Raiders tight end Brock Bowers.

Gardner-Johnson, who was ejected from the game , took responsibility for his actions after the game saying, "I've gotta be a better player. I've gotta be a better vet."

articles.title: Will Jordyn Tyson play in Paris? Saints GM Mickey Loomis shares update
articles.summary: New Orleans Saints general manager Mickey Loomis shared an update on Jordyn Tyson’s injury and status for Sunday’s game with the Steelers in Paris.
articles.body:
New Orleans Saints fans will have to wait until after the bye week to see their team's first-round draft pick Jordyn Tyson. While the rookie wide receiver did travel with the team to Paris ahead of Sunday's game with the Pittsburgh Steelers, longtime general manager Mickey Loomis told reporters Wednesday that Tyson will not be activated from injured reserve just yet.

"He's improving, but he is not going to practice this week," Loomis said. He stressed that Tyson's hamstring injury was not related to the issues he dealt with in college, but acknowledged the team is taking a cautious approach with him: "Hopefully this is the one and only injury he has."

Tyson impressed at training camp until he suffered a hamstring injury during a joint practice session with the Jacksonville Jaguars during the preseason, which landed him on injured reserve to start his rookie year. He missed several games during his final season with Arizona State with another hamstring injury, which lingered into the spring and kept him from participating at the NFL Scouting Combine as well as the Saints' offseason program. He can make plays. The only question is how much time he can spend on the field.

articles.title: What makes Troy Aikman such an appealing option for CBS?
articles.summary: ProShooter/Depositphotos Troy Aikman’s ESPN deal ends in 2027 Troy Kenneth Aikman works as an NFL analyst for ESPN after playing quarterback for the Dallas C...
articles.body:
Troy Kenneth Aikman works as an NFL analyst for ESPN after playing quarterback for the Dallas Cowboys. His current broadcasting agreement runs through Super Bowl LXI, scheduled for February 2027.

During an October 15 radio interview in Dallas, Aikman said he expected to become a free agent. CBS has surfaced as a possible destination, but no agreement has been announced.

CBS and Tony Romo mutually agreed to end their nine-year broadcasting partnership on October 2, 2026. The former Cowboys quarterback had served as the network's lead NFL analyst since 2017.

For nine seasons, Romo worked with play-by-play announcer Jim Nantz on CBS's leading NFL games. The company has not publicly named a permanent replacement for him beyond the current season.

J.J. Watt remains CBS's lead NFL analyst through the 2026 season, joining Jim Nantz and reporter Tracy Wolfson. The network confirmed that lineup when announcing Tony Romo's October 2 departure.

Watt joined CBS's studio coverage in 2023 and later called games alongside Ian Eagle. Before broadcasting, he played 12 seasons with Houston and Arizona, recording 114.5 sacks across his career.

Aikman is in his 26th season of NFL TV work

Aikman joined Fox's NFL coverage in 2001 after retiring as the Dallas Cowboys' quarterback. In 2002, he joined Joe Buck and Cris Collinsworth in a three-person commentary team.

Buck and Aikman began working as a two-person team in 2005. After 21 seasons at Fox, Aikman moved to ESPN in 2022. The 2026 season is his 26th as an NFL analyst and his 25th alongside Buck.

Aikman's broadcast record spans playoffs

Aikman and Buck have called more than 400 NFL regular-season games together. Their partnership has also covered over 40 playoff matchups, including appearances on both Fox and ESPN since 2002.

They covered 18 NFC Championship Games and six Super Bowls during their Fox years. Their final Super Bowl for that network featured Kansas City and San Francisco in February 2020.

The Dallas Cowboys selected Troy Aikman first overall in the 1989 NFL Draft. He guided the team to three Super Bowl championships and earned game MVP honors in January 1993.

During 12 seasons, Aikman passed for 32,942 yards and 165 touchdowns. He made six Pro Bowls before entering the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2006, after his 2001 retirement.

Jim Nantz joined CBS in 1985 and became its lead NFL play-by-play announcer in 2004. By February 2024, he had called seven Super Bowls, including Super Bowl LVIII in Las Vegas.

Nantz spent 13 seasons alongside former Giants quarterback Phil Simms in CBS's lead NFL booth. His career includes four Emmy Awards, including recognition for his role in CBS's Super Bowl LVIII coverage in 2024.

Troy Aikman was selected for the Sports Broadcasting Hall of Fame's 2026 class, announced September 9. The 10 inductees include former Disney CEO Robert Iger and ESPN technician Jim Dove.

The honor recognizes Aikman's work covering games rather than his accomplishments as a quarterback. Organizers scheduled the induction ceremony for December 15 at the New York Hilton Hotel in Manhattan.

ESPN signed Troy Aikman to a reported five-year, $90 million broadcasting contract in 2022. The agreement averages $18 million annually for his work analyzing Monday Night Football games on television.

Joe Buck signed a reported six-year, $108 million extension with ESPN in September 2026, averaging $18 million annually. Aikman remained without an equivalent renewal offer by the middle of October.

Reports described an argument between ESPN broadcasters Joe Buck and Troy Aikman before the October 12 meeting between the Buffalo Bills and Los Angeles Rams at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood.

Contract talks reportedly prompted the exchange. Both worked that evening's broadcast, and Aikman declined to describe the disagreement in detail during an October 15 interview with a Dallas radio station.

Fun fact: Troy Aikman used to read critical social media comments aloud during car rides after games, teasing Joe Buck until his broadcast partner begged him to stop.

CBS averaged 21.252 million viewers for its 2025 NFL regular-season broadcasts. The network's national Sunday game window at 4:25 p.m. ET averaged 25.827 million viewers, ranking as the most-watched program on television.

At the halfway point of the 2026 college football season, the top NFL draft prospects are starting to emerge.

ESPN's Field Yates unveiled his latest mock draft for the top 10 picks in 2027, and he predicted that Oklahoma State's Drew Mestemaker will be the first quarterback off the board. The full top 10 is as follows:

Los Angeles Chargers: Jeremiah Smith, WR, Ohio State

Miami Dolphins: Drew Mestemaker, QB, Oklahoma State

Tennessee Titans: Leonard Moore, CB, Notre Dame

Tampa Bay Buccaneers: Colin Simmons, Edge, Texas

Washington Commanders: Dylan Stewart, Edge, South Carolina

Philadelphia Eagles: Charlie Becker, WR, Indiana

New York Jets (via DAL): C.J. Carr, QB, Notre Dame

Houston Texans: Trevor Goosby, OT, Texas

Arizona Cardinals: Trinidad Chambliss, QB, Ole Miss

New York Jets: Ashton Hampton, CB, Clemson

Mestemaker has shot up draft boards thanks to his scorching start for the Cowboys, throwing for 1,940 yards, 16 touchdowns and six interceptions through six games.

"The 20-year-old Mestemaker oozes upside, as the 6-3 215-pounder is a legitimate dual-threat player with exceptional creativity inside and outside of the pocket," Yates said. "... Despite not starting at quarterback in high school, Mestemaker has shown enough in just two college seasons -- one at North Texas -- to contend for the No. 1 pick. He is a fearless playmaker who can impact nearly every blade of grass on the field with his mobility and off-platform throwing skills."

After Mestemaker, Notre Dame's CJ Carr and Ole Miss' Trinidad Chambliss were the other quarterbacks projected to be selected in the top 10. Texas' Arch Manning and Oregon's Dante Moore, who entered the season pegged as the top two quarterback prospects in the nation, were absent from Yates' list.

The second half of the college football season could give some prospects the chance to improve their draft stock, but it's clear that the 2027 class is filled with talented players who deserve to be selected in the top 10.

articles.title: Jalen Hurts' Camp Reportedly Felt Eagles' Roseman Was 'Exceptional' with Process Around Injury
articles.summary: Philadelphia Eagles general manager Howie Roseman has reportedly received high marks from Jalen Hurts' camp in the wake of the star quarterback's recent health and injury woes.
articles.body:
Philadelphia Eagles general manager Howie Roseman has reportedly received high marks from Jalen Hurts' camp in the wake of the star quarterback's recent health and injury woes.

Per ESPN's Jeremy Fowler , Hurts' team feels that Roseman has been "exceptional" throughout this process.

"He was 'extremely hands on' throughout, 'worried about Jalen's health more than anything else,' the source added," per Fowler.

Hurts was ruled out for the remainder of the season on Monday after the Eagles and Hurts' agent, Nicole Lynn, said in a statement that he has been diagnosed with blood clots in his lungs.

It was previously revealed Hurts played in the Eagles' Week 5 game against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London with a superficial blood clot in his calf. The clot developed after he was cleated the previous week against the Los Angeles Rams.

The timing of the Eagles' announcing Hurts' diagnosis has led to scrutiny about the organization's handling of the situation. Jonathan Jones of The Athletic reported on Tuesday the NFL won't discipline the Eagles after conducting an investigation into the matter.

However, the NFL Players Association issued a statement soon after asking for a "full investigation" into the medical care Hurts received.

The NFLPA noted it was "not aware" of any investigation by the NFL, and the league "previously informed the union that it did not plan to review the care (Hurts) received."

Hurts appeared in five games for the Eagles this season. He threw for 933 yards, eight touchdowns and completed 57.8 percent of his attempts.

Philadelphia has lost four straight games after a 2-0 start. The four-game losing streak is the longest for the franchise since 2020.

articles.title: New NFL Trade Rumors on Potential Rams Deal for WR After Davante Adams' Injury
articles.summary: After placing star receiver Davante Adams on injured reserve due to a hamstring injury, the Los Angeles Rams reportedly will be looking for a replacement.
articles.body:
After placing star receiver Davante Adams on injured reserve due to a hamstring injury, the Los Angeles Rams reportedly will be looking for a replacement.

ESPN's Dan Graziano reported that the Rams are expected to scour the trade market for a wide receiver in hopes of salvaging their season.

"I do not expect the Rams to go down without a fight, and my understanding is that they will at least explore the possibility of trading for a wide receiver in the wake of the Davante Adams injury," Graziano stated. "The issue, of course, is that they don't have a ton to trade."

Graziano went on to explain that Los Angeles' offseason wheeling and dealing left the team without assets to play with ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline.

"They are without their first-round pick in the 2027 draft as a result of the Myles Garrett trade. They are without their third-round pick in that same draft as a result of the Trent McDuffie trade. And they're missing their second-round pick in 2028 and their third-round pick in 2029, both also as a result of the Garrett trade," Graziano stated. "Could the Rams make a player-for-player swap of some sort? Would a team be interested in backup QB Stetson Bennett if the Rams decide rookie Ty Simpson is ready to be Matthew Stafford's backup?"

Rams head coach Sean McVay announced on Monday that Adams is expected to miss six to 10 weeks after suffering a ruptured hamstring in the fourth quarter of Sunday's 18-16 loss to the Arizona Cardinals. A source told ESPN's Jeremy Fowler that Adams "hopes to return on the front end of the six- to 10-week time frame, as close to the post-Week 11 bye as possible."

At 2-4, the Rams have struggled to live up to expectations after entering the season as the Super Bowl favorites. Still, Graziano noted that Los Angeles hasn't lost confidence, stating, "This is a Rams team that had the highest of hopes for 2026 and still believes it can play well enough to salvage this season."

The Rams will try to start building momentum when they meet the Las Vegas Raiders (3-3) in Week 7.

articles.title: NFL Insiders Sound Off on Vita Vea, More Potential 'Sleeper' Trade Targets Ahead of 2026 Deadline
articles.summary: The resolution of contract talks between the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Vita Vea has not stopped the veteran defensive tackle from remaining the subject of trade speculation.
articles.body:
The resolution of contract talks between the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Vita Vea has not stopped the veteran defensive tackle from remaining the subject of trade speculation.

ESPN's Dan Graziano named Vea as a "sleeper name" to be moved ahead of the Nov. 10 deadline.

Here's a look at some of the players Graziano and ESPN's Jeremy Fowler named as underrated trade targets ahead of the trade deadline.

Vea is signed through the 2027 campaign after securing $23 million in salary next season in a deal Graziano described as the Buccaneers coming short of guaranteeing Vea as "part of their long-term future."

The 31-year-old has recorded 13 tackles and three quarterback hits while playing 73 percent of the Bucs' defensive snaps during his team's 1-5 start to the season.

"If you need interior D-line help right now and don't mind paying Vea $23 million next season at age 32, why not call to see what it would take to get him out of Tampa?" Graziano wrote.

Graziano also described Teller and Woolen as "potentially available."

Teller, is playing in his ninth NFL season and first with the Texans (2-4), is signed through 2027. The 31-year-old has allowed one sack on 142 offensive snaps played, per PFF .

Woolen, a 27-year-old playing on an expiring deal, has allowed 15 catches while playing almost every defensive snap for the Eagles (2-4).

Fowler reported that although he doesn't think the Titans are "floating" Taylor as a trade target, the cornerback could be seen as "expendable" after getting benched in Week 6.

Taylor, 27, signed a three-year, $58 million deal with the Titans this offseason but was listed as a healthy scratch before his team claimed their first win of the season Sunday over the Indianapolis Colts.

Fowler also speculated a team could also attempt to see if the Falcons could be willing to move a former Pro Bowler in Bates after a 2-4 start to the season.

"I doubt Atlanta wants to trade him, but his value would be strong if that changes," Fowler reported.

Bates, 29, is another player on an expiring contract. He has made 31 tackles, two passes defensed, one forced fumble and one fumble returned for a touchdown through six games of his fourth season with the Falcons.

The window to trade NFL players this season closes Nov. 10. Los Angeles Chargers edge rusher Khalil Mack, Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr. and Eagles guard Landon Dickerson were ranked as the top three most likely players to move ahead of that deadline in Bleacher Report's latest trade block big board .

articles.title: New Cowboys Rumors Reveal Team's Stance on Trade for Defensive Help Amid Struggles
articles.summary: ESPN's Jeremy Fowler thinks the Dallas Cowboys might be done making big moves on defense after a 2-4 start to the 2026 season.
articles.body:
ESPN's Jeremy Fowler thinks the Dallas Cowboys might be done making big moves on defense after a 2-4 start to the 2026 season.

According to Fowler, "a source told me a trade to aid the Cowboys defense is not a front-burner issue at the moment."

"So, Dallas will always explore a potential move, but it's quite possible the franchise holds onto whatever 2027 draft capital it has left," Fowler reported.

Cowboys owner Jerry Jones spoke about the team's strategy ahead of the deadline, downplaying the idea that the team could be a seller despite its struggles:

The Cowboys currently hold three picks in the 2027 draft. That includes the Green Bay Packers' first-round selection as well as their own second and a Pittsburgh Steelers fourth, according to Tankathon .

Other selections in the upcoming draft were already traded away as part of owner and general manager Jerry Jones' previous deals for defensive tackle Quinnen Williams, offensive tackle Broderick Jones, edge rusher Rashan Gary and wide receiver George Pickens.

Adding players like Williams and Gary has yet to help the Cowboys recover from the exit of Micah Parsons. The Cowboys' defense has allowed the third-most points, and seventh-most yards, in the NFL so far this season.

That's not the Cowboys' only issue. Dallas has also been held below 20 points in each of the team's last two games, most recently getting shut out last Sunday in the first half of a 23-13 Week 6 loss at the Green Boy Packers.

The Cowboys have three games remaining against the Philadelphia Eagles, Arizona Cardinals and Indianapolis Colts, all of which currently have matching 2-4 records, ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline.

A three-game win streak would be enough to put the Cowboys at 5-4, which could be enough to challenge for a division title in an NFC East weakened by multiple season-ending quarterback injuries and increase the odds Jones is willing to add help ahead of the deadline.

Should the Cowboys end up closer to 2-7 by mid-November, however, Jones could look to add to his weak 2027 draft stock by selling off some of his players.

One notable trade target in that case would be Pickens, who is playing this season on a one-year franchise tag after failing to reach resolution on a longer-team extension ahead of the season.

The Cowboys will get their next opportunity to influence which direction Jones takes a the deadline when kicking off a Week 7 matchup against the Eagles next Monday at 8:15 p.m. ET in Philadelphia.

articles.title: New Colts Rumors on Potential Trade Plans at 2026 Deadline After Firing GM Chris Ballard
articles.summary: After Indianapolis Colts general manager Chris Ballard was fired on Monday, the team reportedly could be forced to ship away some key players.
articles.body:
After Indianapolis Colts general manager Chris Ballard was fired on Monday, the team reportedly could be forced to ship away some key players.

ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported that "rival teams believe Indianapolis will be open for business" ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline.

Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon said in her statement after firing Ballard, "We have a lot of football in front of us, and I expect us to compete, improve and win football games." However, the team has a tough slate with upcoming matchups against the Minnesota Vikings, Jacksonville Jaguars and Dallas Cowboys.

Fowler pointed out, "If Indy can find a way to steal two wins in that slate, perhaps that affects trade plans. But this iteration of the Colts does not look poised for upsets, so perhaps change is inevitable."

The Colts have multiple key players on contracts that expire at the end of the season, including offensive lineman Quenton Nelson, defensive linemen DeForest Buckner and Grover Stewart, and wide receivers Josh Downs and Keenan Allen. Indianapolis gave up its 2027 first-round pick in last year's trade to acquire cornerback Sauce Gardner, so the team could look to recoup some draft capital by trading its veterans.

"What Indianapolis does with Nelson will be fascinating," Fowler stated. "He's a legacy Colt, a 2018 first-round draft pick and frequent All-Pro. But the team did not aggressively pursue an extension this summer, and rarely do premier O-linemen become available at the deadline. Also, defensive tackle Jerry Tillery is a name to watch."

articles.title: J.J. McCarthy Reportedly Named Giants QB1 Over Jameis Winston for Giants' NFL Week 7 Game vs. Texans
articles.summary: The New York Giants reportedly have a new starter under center.
articles.body:
The New York Giants reportedly have a new starter under center.

According to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler , the Giants plan to start J.J. McCarthy at quarterback over Jameis Winston for a Week 7 matchup with the Houston Texans.

New York initially acquired McCarthy in a trade with the Minnesota Vikings on Sept. 28, sending out a 2027 fifth-round draft pick in exchange for the signal-caller.

He served as a depth piece for the Giants before entering their first-team offense after Winston was benched in the second half of a 34-27 loss to the New Orleans Saints in Week 6.

McCarthy didn't get off to a hot start against New Orleans, as he threw an interception on his first drive of the game.

Still, he bounced back and nearly helped the Giants pull off an improbable comeback victory. They trailed 34-10 at the time McCarthy entered the game in the fourth quarter before cutting the deficit to 34-27.

New York also had an opportunity to tie the game on its final possession, but couldn't convert on fourth down at the Saints' 14-yard line.

McCarthy finished 11-of-21 for 243 yards and one touchdown while getting picked off once, as Winston went 14-of-26 for 152 yards and one touchdown compared to a pair of interceptions.

McCarthy is looking to get is career back on track, as the former first-round pick failed to meet expectations as a member of the Vikings.

In 2024, he was sidelined for his entire rookie season due to a torn meniscus .

McCarthy struggled the following year, completing 57.6 percent of his passes for 1,632 yards and 11 touchdowns to go along with 12 interceptions in 10 games. He was also unable to beat out Kyler Murray in a training camp battle for Minnesota's first-string quarterback job heading into his 2026 campaign.

As for Winston, he's started in each of the Giants' four games since Jaxson Dart suffered a season-ending knee injury in Week 2.

Winston has thrown for 957 yards, seven touchdowns and five interceptions while posting a 57.0 completion percentage.

The Giants have still opened their 2026 season on a high note despite utilizing multiple starting quarterbacks, sitting atop the NFC East standings with a 3-2-1 record.

They'll face the Texans on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Apollo, Blackstone Have NFL Aspirations, Seek Approval to Buy Stakes in Teams
articles.summary: Blackstone Inc. and a unit of Apollo Global Management Inc. are in talks with the NFL to join the league’s list of approved private equity firms that can tak...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Blackstone Inc. and a unit of Apollo Global Management Inc. are in talks with the NFL to join the league's list of approved private equity firms that can take minority stakes in its teams, according to people familiar with the matter.

The discussions are preliminary and both firms would likely need to find a deal with a team before completing the approval process, said the people, who weren't authorized to speak publicly about the talks. Approval isn't imminent and completion of the process would likely come next year, according to one of the people.

Another person familiar with the talks said the NFL has been in communication with multiple private equity firms, and that the league's owners have been pleased with its private equity partners so far.

The NFL, Blackstone and Apollo declined to comment.

The league began its private equity policy two years ago, giving owners more opportunities to raise capital for stadium projects and estate management. The shift also further boosted team valuations. The Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks recently changed hands for a record $9.6 billion, topping the Washington Commanders sale in 2023 for about $6 billion.

Apollo Sports Capital, an Apollo division created last year, has invested or committed to $13 billion of deals, according to Al Tylis, its chief executive officer. In September at Bloomberg Power Players New York, he said that "we're interested in any great sports property anywhere in the world, which clearly includes the NFL."

Blackstone and CVC Capital were previously on the list of approved investors as part of a consortium alongside the Carlyle Group and Dynasty Equity Partners, but both pulled out. In Blackstone's latest attempt, the firm would enter the league's private equity policy on its own.

Firms such as Arctos Partners, Ares Management, Sixth Street and a partnership between Carlyle Group and Dynasty Equity Partners have bought into NFL clubs. Arctos has led the way, buying stakes in four teams including the Buffalo Bills and Los Angeles Chargers.

articles.title: Roger Goodell: 'We welcome' NFLPA call for investigation into Jalen Hurts' blood clots
articles.summary: Questions swirled regarding the safety of Hurts playing and traveling on a seven-plus hour transatlantic flight with the clots.
articles.body:
NEW YORK — After the NFL Players Association called for an investigation into the handling of Jalen Hurts' blood clots , commissioner Roger Goodell said Wednesday "we welcome that."

"That's fine," Goodell said. "Our chief medical officers have been through the protocols that were followed. So we welcome that. That's what they did, they have that right."

Hurts was diagnosed Oct. 10 with a superficial blood clot on his calf and then played the Jacksonville Jaguars in London on Oct. 11. In the days that followed last week, doctors found the blood clot had moved not only into the deep veins of his calf but also into both of his lungs.

The Eagles placed him on injured reserve as he undergoes treatment with blood thinners.

Questions swirled regarding the safety of Hurts playing and traveling on a seven-plus hour transatlantic flight with the clots. NFL executive vice president Jeff Miller denounced Tuesday what he called "the unfounded criticism that was leveled against" team doctors in response to Hurts' progressed condition.

The NFLPA called Tuesday night for an investigation.

The union issued a statement Tuesday evening demanding more transparency.

"The NFLPA is not aware of any NFL investigations into the medical care provided to Jalen Hurts," the union said in a statement. "In fact, the league previously informed the union that it did not plan to review the care he received.

"Before conclusions are drawn about how this situation was handled, there must be a full investigation into what occurred. Determining the facts is essential to ensuring players receive the highest level of care and protection going forward."

Goodell reiterated Wednesday that "I think our protocols were incredibly good there."

"The most important thing here is Jalen's health, ultimately …" Goodell said. "I'm more worried about his health ultimately, but the protocols were followed."

articles.title: Titans' Jordan Elliott was released after reportedly going to retrieve a gun after dispute at practice
articles.summary: Jordan Elliott lasted just five games with the Titans.
articles.body:
The Tennessee Titans unceremoniously released offseason acquisition Jordan Elliott on Tuesday. The team's statement on the transaction was just 41 words long, and was devoid of specific details, merely citing an " incident at our team facility ."

Details of the "incident" have since come to light, with reports suggesting Elliott was released after allegedly going to retrieve a gun from his car following a practice altercation with a teammate, per KPRC2 reporter Aaron Wilson. That report was confirmed by NFL Network's Mike Garafolo and the Athletic's Jonathan Jones on Wednesday.

While the NFL has not directly confirmed the incident, an NFL spokesperson told Pro Football Talk the situation was " under review ." NFL players are prohibited from having firearms at team or league facilities, so Elliott could face additional punishment from the league if the report is true.

Titans head coach Robert Saleh seemed to confirm that report Wednesday, saying Elliott " pulled a gun in the parking lot." Saleh ultimately went to bat for Elliott, calling him a "great man" and a "great father."

Saleh said he viewed Elliott's actions as a "cry for help" and brought up NFL players who died by suicide over the past year. Saleh said he didn't want to speculate on whether Elliott was in the same place, but said those situations are an example of how much NFL players endure mentally and physically.

Saleh then said he would be happy to go to bat for Elliott if any other team is looking to pick him up. Saleh again called Elliott a "great man" who "had a terrible lapse in judgment."

On Thursday, Elliott and offensive tackle JC Latham were reportedly involved in a dispute at practice that resulted in Elliott being told to leave the field, per Wilson. Elliott, 28, then reportedly took off his pads and went to his car to retrieve a gun, possibly to confront Latham. The entire sequence was reportedly captured by security cameras at the team's facility.

It does not appear a confrontation took place as defensive lineman John Franklin-Myers was reportedly able to talk Elliott down. The gun reportedly never left Elliott's parking spot, per Garafolo.

Following the alleged incident, Elliott did not practice with the team the following day. At the time, Saleh said the defensive tackle was "dealing with personal stuff."

Elliott was inactive for the team's Week 6 win over the Indianapolis Colts and was released a few days later.

Elliott was expected to be a useful contributor to the Titans after signing a two-year, $8.5 million deal with the team in the offseason. The defensive tackle followed Saleh to the Titans from the San Francisco 49ers, so the head coach clearly saw something in Elliott's ability.

In five games, Elliott registered 11 total tackles.

If the details surrounding Elliott's release are true, it's hard to see the former third-round draft pick hooking on with another NFL team in the immediate future.

articles.title: Sam LaPorta Says He Broke His 'F--king Back' for Lions, Sounds Off on Lack of New Contract
articles.summary: Detroit Lions tight end Sam LaPorta wasn't pleased about the lack of a contract extension as he navigates through the 2026 season.
articles.body:
Detroit Lions tight end Sam LaPorta wasn't pleased about the lack of a contract extension as he navigates through the 2026 season.

"I think the combination of getting your heartstrings twisted as well as the violent sport we play—it sucks," LaPorta said during a Wednesday appearance on Pardon My Take (h/t Pride of Detroit's Jeremy Reisman ). "It's disappointing that you go out there every week and you bear the risk of getting hurt. Like last year, whatever it was, Week 9, Week 10, I break my f--king back for this team. And then I'm going out there this year, and I'm ballin', and maybe they're just not showing the love."

The 25-year-old previously underwent season-ending surgery to repair a fully herniated disc in Nov. 2025.

On Oct. 4, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported that LaPorta and the Lions broke off extension negotiations.

"So I'm going to continue to do my thing and ball out, and in three months if I don't get to wear the Honolulu Blue and play for the Lions anymore, it's going to be all good," LaPorta said Wednesday. "I'll go get paid somewhere else. So, whatever."

He's currently playing on the final year of his rookie contract .

The 25-year-old previously weighed in on contract discussions with Detroit on Oct. 7.

"I don't know if it's truly off the table, but I think there's certainly a stalemate right now and I'm really giving the reigns to my agent Jack Bechta," LaPorta said at the time, per ESPN's Eric Woodyard . "He's been handling it with the front office and all the advice he's given me so far is just that we haven't come to terms yet. That's about it."

He was initially selected by the Lions with a second-round pick in the 2023 NFL draft before putting together a rookie season in which he caught 86 passes for 889 yards and 10 touchdowns.

He earned a Pro Bowl nod as well as a Second Team All-Pro selection for his efforts.

LaPorta's production dipped slightly the following year, although he still hauled in 60 receptions for 726 yards and seven scores.

He went on to record 489 yards on 40 catches across nine games during his shortened 2025 campaign.

This year, LaPorta ranks No. 5 among all tight ends with 316 receiving yards in five games. He's also found the end zone three times.

Lions quarterback Jared Goff owns a 139.1 passer rating when targeting LaPorta, according to Pro Football Focus .

Detroit currently owns a 3-2 record, but sits at No. 4 in the NFC North standings.

As LaPorta looks to help the Lions contend for a playoff berth, he's also searching for a new contract.

articles.summary: Tampa Bay Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles revealed that he'll make a decision regarding quarterback Baker Mayfield's availability on Friday ahead of a Week 7 matchup with the Carolina Panthers, per ESPN's Jenna Laine.
articles.body:
Tampa Bay Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles revealed that he'll make a decision regarding quarterback Baker Mayfield's availability on Friday ahead of a Week 7 matchup with the Carolina Panthers, per ESPN's Jenna Laine .

Mayfield has missed each of Tampa Bay's past three games due to a dislocated right thumb that he suffered during a Week 3 loss to the Minnesota Vikings, but returned to practice on Wednesday.

Bowles explained that Mayfield threw the ball well during Wednesday's session and did well in what he was asked to do, per Laine.

If the signal-caller isn't able to suit up against Carolina, the Buccaneers will stick with Jalon Daniels under center.

Daniels, an undrafted rookie, has appeared in four total games this season. He's completed 61.2 percent of his throws for 501 yards and three touchdowns compared to five interceptions.

As for Mayfield, health woes haven't kept him off the field during his tenure in Tampa Bay prior to the thumb injury. He didn't miss a game across his first three seasons on the Buccaneers from 2023-25.

If the two-time Pro Bowler is able to return against Carolina, it would mark a relatively swift recovery.

ESPN's Adam Schefter previously reported that Mayfield was expected to be sidelined "anywhere from three to six weeks, depending on how quickly he is able to grip the football."

The veteran passer wore a glove on his throwing hand in Wednesday's practice while taking snaps, throwing and participating in ball security drills.

Mayfield dealt with some inconsistency to open his 2026 campaign prior to the injury, completing 63.5 percent of his passes for 615 yards and two touchdowns while getting picked off twice in three contests. He also lost three fumbles.

articles.title: Goodell says NFL is comfortable with security around Sunday’s Paris game amid protests
articles.summary: The NFL’s comfort level with security around the upcoming game in Paris is “very high” despite the ongoing protests in France, commissioner Roger Goodell said at league meetings on Wednesday.
articles.body: The NFL’s comfort level with security for the upcoming game in Paris is “very high” despite the ongoing protests in France, commissioner Roger Goodell said at the league meetings on Wednesday. But with unrest in the city expected to surge on Saturday, Goodell said of the potential need for a last-minute pivot, “We’ll deal with that.” Last weekend, more than 2,000 people were arrested in Paris as part of widespread protests over the cost of living and the state of education in France. There were at least two deaths and reports of serious injuries. The Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints are scheduled to play on Sunday at the Stade de France just outside of the capital. The league has been on the ground for well over a week, working closely with both the Parisian authorities and the State Department. Goodell said he had a conversation with Secretary of State Marco Rubio just a few days ago. On Tuesday, Peter O’Reilly, the NFL’s head of international affairs, said, “All of our plans for the Paris game this weekend are moving forward as planned.” He also said that while they have contingency plans for every game, they’ve yet to seriously consider relocating the game from the Stade de France, the national stadium that hosted major events during the 2024 Olympics. The NFL is playing a record-high nine international games this season as part of a concerted push to market the game globally. The collective bargaining agreement between the league and its players union allows the league to schedule up to 10 international games in a season, and O’Reilly said they are considering playing that many in 2027. “All of our events we have going on, we always have a very strong security presence around all of those events,” O’Reilly said. “And that presence will be heightened with local authorities making sure that there’s nothing more important from our standpoint than the team security, the fan security, everybody involved with this game.” O’Reilly acknowledged that ensuring the NFL doesn’t deplete local security resources required elsewhere to quell violence is “a very important factor.” “As we stand here right now, we feel confident that we would not have any impact on the broader resources needed,” he said. French authorities have implemented a curfew and expect a significant protest this Saturday. “We’ve made all the preparations. We’ve been in touch with the appropriate authorities,” Goodell said. “Protests are not unusual in France.” The matchup between the Steelers and Saints will be the first NFL game in France. “We look forward to it,” Goodell said, “and I’m leaving shortly to go myself.”

articles.title: EA Sports Confirms It's Developing an Open-World Football Game
articles.summary: EA Sports is working on a new open-world football game, seemingly separate from Madden and College Football.
articles.body:
EA Sports is working on a new open-world football game, seemingly separate from Madden and College Football.

In a new letter about EA's future , the company outlined what's on the horizon for its different portfolios. For its sports games, the publisher reaffirmed that it is working on a brand new Fight Night game , which will be EA's first boxing game in well over a decade. However, the more interesting announcement is that EA is working on a new open-world football game that it calls "Project Gridiron."

"We have two new projects in development you’ll hear about over the next few months, including a brand-new, social-first open-world experience for our American Football team that we call 'Project Gridiron,'" said EA. "And we are also in pre-production to bring back a beloved, fan-favorite in Fight Night, leveraging capabilities from our simulation fighting team."

EA Sports College Football 27 - Dynasty Screenshots and GIFs

It's unclear if Project Gridiron will have some kind of narrative or if its open-world will be a shared online universe, not unlike NBA 2K. Could this be a more mature and gritty football game, similar to what Fight Night Champion did for that series? It's hard to say right now. Madden briefly dabbled with narrative-driven campaigns in the mid to late 2010s with decent results, but eventually turned its focus back toward a broader career mode for those looking for a progressive single-player experience.

While a new College Football is expected to release next year per previous statements from EA Sports , the existence of Project Gridiron creates a question over whether or not Madden will be benched in favor of this new game.

After all, does anyone have the time, money, or interest in three EA-developed football games in a single year? It's also possible this is a total transformation of the Madden experience, but it sounds like something brand new. It sounds like we won't have to wait too long, as EA noted we will learn more about the game in the "next few months." Perhaps we'll hear about this during The Game Awards or sometime in early 2027, but we'll just have to wait and see.

A recent report also noted that there was some internal concern over the future of College Football , as the rising costs for NIL rights, in addition to other licensing and development expenses, are creating friction. The series' sales have reportedly declined year by year, leading some developers to worry the franchise's return may be relatively short-lived. Perhaps Project Gridiron could replace College Football in the future.

articles.title: Allen Bailey Dies at 37, Former NFL DE Played for Chiefs and Falcons

articles.body:
Former NFL defensive end Allen Bailey, who played for the Kansas City Chiefs and Atlanta Falcons, has died at the age of 37.

Chiefs head coach Andy Reid, who coached Bailey from 2013 to 2018, confirmed the news during his press conference on Wednesday.

"Sad news, the passing of Allen Bailey. Our hearts go out to his family. Prayers are with them. Way too young, obviously," Reid said. "One of my favorite players. Great kid, and just sorry to see that happen to him."

Alford Bailey Jr., Allen's brother, told TMZ Sports Allen's body was discovered in his Florida home on Tuesday. The cause of death has not yet been announced.

Bailey was a third-round pick by the Chiefs in the 2011 NFL draft. He played four years in college at the University of Miami from 2007 to 2010 and was named to the All-ACC team in his final two seasons.

The Georgia native appeared in all 16 games with Kansas City as a rookie. He spent the first eight years of his NFL career with the Chiefs. His best season came in 2018 when he recorded six sacks to help the team reach the AFC Championship Game.

Following the 2018 campaign, Bailey signed a two-year contract with the Falcons in free agency. He appeared in 31 games with Atlanta before being released by the club in February 2021.

articles.title: Fantasy Football Week 7 Start 'Em, Sit 'Em: A.J. Brown vs. Luther Burden III
articles.summary: Evaluating who to play in fantasy football this week between Patriots WR A.J. Brown and Bears WR Luther Burden III.
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears and the New England Patriots will face off on Thursday Night Football this week. That game brings forth two WRs with high-scoring fantasy potential: Chicago Bears WR Luther Burden III and New England Patriots WR A.J. Brown. Here is a breakdown of who fantasy managers should have in their starting lineups in Week 7 between Brown and Burden III.

With QB Caleb Williams back in the Bears' lineup in Week 6 against the Atlanta Falcons, his favorite targets were TE Colston Loveland and Burden III. In the contest, Burden III had eight receptions for 95 yards. Impressively, he did that while playing in a season-low 39% of snaps.

Burden III's Week 7 opponent, the Patriots, do have an above-average passing defense. They are currently allowing the 11th fewest passing yards per game in the NFL, 209.0. Despite that, they have shown they can give up big games to opposing pass catchers of late. In their past three games, a player has recorded over 100 receiving yards against them-Buffalo Bills WR Keon Coleman, Las Vegas Raiders TE Brock Bowers, and New York Jets WR Omar Cooper Jr.

A negative, though, is that the Patriots' last three opponents have not overly used their pass game. They averaged 30.3 pass attempts per game against New England. When comparing that to the NFL teams' average pass attempts per game for 2026, that average would rank as the 10th fewest attempts per game in the league.

Brown made his return to the Patriots lineup in Week 6 against the New York Jets, after sustaining an ankle injury in Week 1 that kept him sidelined. In his first game back, he did not play well. He had just three receptions for 27 yards. And although fantasy managers might be panicking given the ADP Brown had and the production he has put forth thus far, there were still some positives to take away from Week 6.

Brown against the Jets led all New England WRs in targets (10) and snap share (76%). He will also have a slightly more favorable fantasy opponent in Week 7 with the Bears.

Chicago this season is allowing the 14th fewest passing yards per game, 211.8. The Bears are giving up the 10th most standard and the 15th most PPR fantasy points per game of any team in the NFL to opposing WRs.

When it comes to who fantasy managers should start in fantasy in Week 7 between Burden III and Brown, they should start Brown.

Brown, even though he has yet to log a big-time fantasy performance, had the volume to do so in Week 6, and that should be the case again in Week 7 against an opponent better for his fantasy outlook: the Bears.

Also, Brown has less competition for targets than Burden III does with Loveland and Odunze. Brown's main competition for targets is WR DeMario Douglas, who has played over 60% of snaps this season just one time. Both Loveland and Odunze combine for just one game where they had less than a 60% snap share.

articles.body:
Colin Kaepernick's jersey appears at Finals

A spectator near the court wore former San Francisco 49ers quarterback Colin Kaepernick's No. 7 jersey during Game 1 of the 2026 WNBA Finals.

The Golden State Valkyries hosted the Atlanta Dream at Chase Center in San Francisco on October 17, 2026. The Spun reported the jersey sighting during Golden State's 68-64 victory in the championship opener.

Colin Kaepernick's jersey draws attention

Sports writer Dan Zaksheske highlighted a spectator wearing Colin Kaepernick's No. 7 jersey during the October 17 WNBA Finals opener. His social media post drew attention to the courtside sighting.

The Spun subsequently covered the photograph and characterized the jersey as a show of support for Kaepernick. The moment involved an individual spectator rather than a formal tribute organized by the WNBA or either of the participating teams.

Colin Kaepernick spent his entire NFL playing career with the San Francisco 49ers, representing the franchise from 2011 through 2016. His professional football career established a connection with sports fans throughout Northern California.

The 49ers currently play their home games at Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara, while the Golden State Valkyries play at Chase Center in San Francisco. Both venues serve professional sports audiences across the Bay Area.

Colin Kaepernick attended 2024 WNBA playoffs

Colin Kaepernick attended Game 2 of the 2024 WNBA semifinal series between the New York Liberty and Las Vegas Aces. The October 1, 2024, matchup took place at Barclays Center in Brooklyn, New York.

During the game, the arena's video screen identified Kaepernick as a former NFL quarterback and activist. According to reporting cited by The Spun, spectators cheered as he smiled and waved toward the crowd.

Colin Kaepernick began protesting racial injustice during the 2016 NFL season while playing quarterback for the San Francisco 49ers. He initially sat during the national anthem before adopting a kneeling demonstration.

Kaepernick explained that his actions addressed racial inequality and police brutality in the United States. Other professional athletes later participated in similar demonstrations, while his decision generated both public support and criticism across American sports.

Colin Kaepernick discusses his NFL absence

Colin Kaepernick has not appeared in an NFL regular-season game since the 2016 season. During a September 2026 interview with NBC News, he discussed his extended absence from professional football and the league.

Kaepernick said he believes his protests contributed to his exclusion from the NFL. He also explained that he watches college football instead of NFL games because of his concerns about the league's treatment of protesting players.

Colin Kaepernick maintains early workouts

Colin Kaepernick continued training regularly in 2026, nearly 10 years after his final NFL regular-season appearance. The former San Francisco 49ers quarterback discussed his fitness routine in interviews published during September.

The Guardian reported that Kaepernick still gets up at approximately 4:30 a.m. each day to train. His regular workouts remain part of his schedule despite not having played in an NFL regular-season game since 2016.

Fun fact: The Golden State Valkyries introduced Violet, a raven mascot nicknamed Vi, during halftime of their game against the Connecticut Sun on August 11, 2025, at Chase Center Ballhalla.

Golden State Valkyries win Finals opener

The Golden State Valkyries defeated the Atlanta Dream 68 to 64 in Game 1 of the 2026 WNBA Finals on October 17. The victory gave Golden State an early lead in the championship series.

According to the WNBA's official game recap, the contest featured 7 lead changes and 6 ties. Golden State closed the game with a 17 to 6 scoring run to secure the franchise's first Finals victory.

Gabby Williams scores 26 points in Game 1

Golden State Valkyries forward Gabby Williams scored 26 points against the Atlanta Dream in the October 17 WNBA Finals opener. Williams led all scorers as Golden State secured a victory at Chase Center.

Williams scored 16 points during the second quarter and made 4 free throws in the final 1 minute and 18 seconds. According to the WNBA, no other Golden State player reached double figures in scoring.

Atlanta Dream forward Angel Reese recorded 14 points and 12 rebounds against the Golden State Valkyries in Game 1 of the 2026 WNBA Finals. Her rebounding performance helped Atlanta compete throughout the championship opener.

Allisha Gray led Atlanta with 19 points after returning from a hand injury that sidelined her during part of the semifinals. Jordin Canada added 8 points, 7 assists, and 5 rebounds for the Dream.

Valkyries reach Finals in their second year

The Golden State Valkyries reached the 2026 WNBA Finals in their second season after beginning league play in 2025. The expansion franchise completed the 2026 regular season with a 32 to 12 record.

Golden State entered the playoffs as the No. 2 seed and swept the defending champion Las Vegas Aces in 3 semifinal games. The Valkyries became the first WNBA expansion franchise to reach the Finals in its second season.

Atlanta Dream tie Finals series at 1 to 1

The Atlanta Dream defeated the Golden State Valkyries 79 to 65 in Game 2 of the WNBA Finals on October 19, 2026. The victory tied the championship series after Golden State won the opener.

Angel Reese led Atlanta with 30 points and 16 rebounds, while Allisha Gray contributed 18 points. According to the WNBA, Reese became the youngest player to record at least 30 points and 15 rebounds in a Finals game.

The 2026 WNBA Finals will continue at 8 p.m. EDT on October 21, when the Atlanta Dream host the Golden State Valkyries in Game 3. The best-of-seven championship series is tied 1-1 entering the game.

Games 3 and 4 are scheduled for State Farm Arena, home of the NBA's Atlanta Hawks. The venue offers substantially more seating than Gateway Center Arena, where the Dream played most of their 2026 home games.

"A couple of other 2026 free agent signings who stand out as potentially available due to their situations not working out include Texans offensive lineman Wyatt Teller and Eagles cornerback Riq Woolen," Graziano writes.

For a team that's struggled with offensive line play the last two seasons, it might seem odd for them to trade a veteran lineman who's a former Pro Bowler.

But with the Texans getting solid play out of Ed Ingram and Keylan Rutledge, Teller has become a bit more expendable than he was before the start of the year.

The 6-foot-4, 315-pound offensive guard is sure to have some suitors interested, as he's a decent veteran and could be a decent starter for a team desperate for OL help.

Houston isn't going to sell him for cheap, however, as their offensive line issues likely won't make them so easily convinced to give up on Teller this season.

But if a contender comes with the right offer, Graziano isn't ruling out a trade of Teller this Fall. It might not be likely, but it does appear that Teller is a name to monitor by the 2026 NFL trade deadline this November.

articles.title: Drake Maye discusses what makes Bears QB Caleb Williams so special
articles.summary: Patriots quarterback Drake Maye complimented Bears quarterback Caleb Williams for his elusiveness ahead of their game on Thursday night.
articles.body:
Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams and New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye will forever be intertwined. They went into college in 2021 and had successful careers before being drafted in the 2024 NFL Draft. Williams was selected No. 1 overall and Maye was selected No. 3 overall.

Now, for the first time since their rookie seasons, these quarterbacks will have the chance to face each other on Thursday Night Football. Maye won that game 19-3. But the Bears are a much different team than they were in 2024 and head coach Ben Johnson's offense allows Williams to do what he does best.

Prior to their game, Maye described what he has seen from Williams in the NFL and what makes him special.

Photos from Bears' 31-23 win over Falcons in Week 6

"He's special in a way he can move and kind of escape and evade pressure and throwing on the run is pretty cool to watch," Maye said. "So I don't know if I'm that shifty in the pocket. He can do some cool things. And he's got crazy arm talent and it's fun to watch. But I wouldn't say it feel - I don't know if I'm that flexible to try some of those things. But I think the way he plays the game is cool. And I know he's doing a great job."

Williams has faced the No. 2 overall pick, Jayden Daniels, twice. Daniels won the first matchup when they were rookies, but Williams got his revenge during the 2025 season in prime time. He will be hoping for the same result on Thursday against Maye.

Both quarterbacks have been playing well as Williams completed over 80 percent of his passes in last week's win against the Atlanta Falcons while Maye has 10 touchdown passes in the past three games.
