articles.title: NFL power rankings round-up 2026: How do Texans fare entering Week 7?
articles.summary: Now sitting at 1-4 following their win over the Tennessee Titans, how much has changed between the public's opinion?
articles.body:
A new-look Houston Texans roster entering mid-October? It seems like it after a win across the pond?

With a game-sealing drive in the fourth quarter, Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud did everything possible to set up Ka'imi Fairbairn in range for a 49-yard game-winning field goal, securing the 34-31 victory over the Jacksonville Jaguars on the slippery grass at Wembley Stadium.

Houston, which has now won back-to-back games, improves to 2-4 overall and 2-1 in the AFC South.

"His mindset was 'Hey, I got you Coach, don't worry about it," Texans coach DeMeco Ryans said of Fairbairn. "When a player tells me that, that just gives me the confidence that I need. He responded in an outstanding way."

The NFL's most clutch kicker was only a footnote in the Texans ' promising outing across the pond. Stroud, who finally threw his first interception after 209 pass attempts, drove down the field with ease, completing 70.6 percent for his passes for 312 yards and three touchdown passes, including two to Foster Moreau in the red zone.

Second-year wide receiver Jaylin Noel gave reason as to why his role should expand in the future, totaling his first 100-yard career outing. The icing on top of the cake? A 13-yard touchdown in the third quarter to extend Houston's lead to 10.

As for the Giants , they're coming off a 34-27 loss at home to the New Orleans Saints , but could have a bit of life with the arrival of new quarterback J.J. McCarthy. The former top-10 pick replaced Jameis Winston down by 24 in the fourth quarter and added a spark following his interception.

He threw for 243 yards and a touchdown while leading two scoring drives to bring New York within a score.

With a win, the Texans would move to 3-4 entering the bye week, which is far from the expected win total at the start of the year, but would mark the start of an actual winning streak. But where do they rank among contenders after a wn in London?

Let's take a quick look at where the Texans sit among NFL power rankings throughout the major publications entering Sunday's matchup at Reliant Stadium.

Nate Davis, USA TODAY: 20 (Last Week 26)

From Davis: "They continue to have one of the league's least-efficient run games. But that defense, QB C.J. Stroud's inspired play and an upgraded wideout corps − not to mention DeMeco Ryans calling the defensive plays again − suggest this team could go on another long heater."

Pete Prisco, CBS Sports: 15 (Last Week 23)

From Prisco: "That was a big-time victory in London over the Jaguars . C.J. Stroud is really playing at a high level, but the defense has to pick it up."

Frank Schwab, Yahoo! Sports: 17 (Last Week 24)

From Schwab: "The 2025 Texans started 0-3, blew out a hapless Titans team, then got a 44-10 win against the Ravens and that led to a 12-5 record and a playoff berth. This season's Texans started 0-4, blew out a hapless Titans team and then got a huge 34-31 win against a good Jaguars team in London. The next four games are vs. Giants, at Chargers, at Browns, vs. Colts. Those teams rank 28th, 31st, 21st and 25th in DVOA. Nothing is guaranteed in the NFL, but there's an opportunity for the Texans to be 6-4 in a month."

From Shook: "Don't look now, but the Texans are clawing their way back into relevance! Houston's defense isn't the shutdown unit it was in years past, but the talent-laden group has inched itself closer to familiarity since DeMeco Ryans took the play-calling reins. Most importantly, C.J. Stroud is playing some of the best football of his career. His performance in London was simply exquisite (save for his late interception in the end zone), and if the Texans can sustain their turnaround, he'll force his way into the MVP conversation."

From The Score: "After fizzling out in Arizona, Marvin Harrison Jr. has a fresh start with the Texans. But make no mistake: There are no excuses this time. The 2024 fourth overall pick needs to deliver on his potential or else he'll quickly start bouncing around the league. Harrison caught three passes for 34 yards in his Texans debut, a win over the Jaguars."

Josh Kendall, The Athletic: 17 (Last Week 21)

From Kendall: "Houston's slow start was not the fault of its quarterback. Stroud, who is in the fourth year of his rookie deal and is headed toward interesting contract negotiations with the Texans, is 16th in the league in fantasy scoring (112.2) and on pace for the best passer rating (100.9) and EPA per dropback (0.15) numbers of his career. The Texans have won two in a row after Sunday's victory in London."

Kristopher Knox, Bleacher Report: 19 (Last Week 24)

From Knox: "Houston's defense hasn't been nearly as dominant as it was a year ago. However, C.J. Stroud is playing at a Pro Bowl level and leads a balanced offense—when healthy—that will give the Texans a chance to win more often than not. New wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. had just three receptions for 34 yards in his Texans debut on Sunday, but he should help open up the passing attack. Climbing out of a2-4 hole will be difficult, of course. However, Houston did exactly that last season and made it to the divisional round. This is a team that must be taken seriously moving forward, even if it is still chasing the early playoff field."

Ralph Vacchiano, FOX Sports: 19 (Last Week 23)

From Vacchiano: "They're baaaaaack! Everyone thought the Texans were dead at 0-4. … OK, I thought they were dead, but I wasn't the only one. But they got right two weeks ago against the awful Titans and stayed right with a terrific 34-31 win in London against the Jaguars. C.J. Stroud finally looks like the franchise QB he was supposed to be. He has plenty of weapons, with the addition of WR Marvin Harrison Jr. But what happened to DeMeco Ryans' defense? It's not nearly as dominant as it once was. If the Texans can fix it, they're a good bet to become the second-ever team to start 0-4 and make the playoffs."

Conor Orr, Sports Illustrated: 14 (Last Week 14)

From Orr: "Forget about the defense. The narrative heading into the trade deadline should be: How much more help can Houston provide C.J. Stroud, who is playing at a top-10 level over the course of the last month and seeing the field better than he has in two years. My take? Call Philadelphia and see what Saquon Barkley has left in the tank."

From Bien-Aime: "The Texans' passing attack is humming, as quarterback C.J. Stroud ranks second league-wide in passing yards (1,712), but an effective run game would take this offense to the top tier. They're averaging 84.8 rushing yards per game (25th) and have 32 rushing first downs on the season (tied for 22nd). Running back David Montgomery, who was acquired via trade in March, is averaging a career-low 2.7 yards per carry and missed Week 6 because of a groin injury. "

Cole Thompson, Texans Wire : 17 (Last Week 19)

From Thompson: "Win a game, trade for a potential game-changing wide receiver. That's what the Texans did after their victory on the road in Nashville. Right now, they're in the race to come back in the AFC South, so trading a second-round pick for WR Marvin Harrison Jr. in theory makes sense. Should Houston lose across the pond, well, at least it has C.J. Stroud's favorite college wideout for the next two seasons.."

articles.title: Rob Gronkowski Makes Bold Drake Maye Claim Ahead of Caleb Williams Showdown
articles.summary: The former Patriots tight end explained why he would take Drake Maye over Caleb Williams, pointing to the New England quarterback’s touch and ability to read...
articles.body:
Former New England Patriots tight end Rob Gronkowski has made his pick in the debate between Drake Maye and Caleb Williams.

With the Patriots preparing to face the Chicago Bears on Thursday night, Gronkowski appeared on "Up & Adams" with Kay Adams and was asked which quarterback he would rather have. Although he acknowledged that both young signal-callers landed in favorable situations, he ultimately gave Maye the edge.

"If I had to choose a quarterback, this is tough, this is tough, it really is, but I'm gonna go with Drake Maye," Gronkowski said.

The four-time Super Bowl champion explained that Maye's throwing and ability to process defenses helped separate him from Williams. He also believes the Patriots quarterback has plenty of room to develop.

"I just like the touch on his ball," Gronkowski said. "And I feel like at the end, Drake Maye would be, for me as a player, he would be the ideal quarterback."

Williams has his own strengths, and Gronkowski made sure to acknowledge the situation surrounding the Chicago quarterback. He praised Bears head coach Ben Johnson for landing in a favorable spot with Williams, noting that an offensive system must fit the quarterback running it.

Still, Gronkowski believes Maye has the advantage heading into Thursday's matchup.

The Patriots and Bears enter the contest with identical 4-2 records, setting up a notable meeting between two of the top quarterbacks from the 2024 NFL Draft. Williams was selected first overall, while New England took Maye with the third pick.

Maye and Williams first met as rookies in November 2024, when New England secured a 19-3 victory in Chicago. The Patriots recorded nine sacks in that game, making it a difficult afternoon for Williams and the Bears' offense.

Their next meeting offers both quarterbacks an opportunity to show how far they have progressed since their rookie seasons. Gronkowski has made his preference clear, but Thursday's game will give Maye and Williams another chance to make their cases on the field.

articles.title: Eagles star TE named fitting trade piece for Seahawks to pursue
articles.summary: The Seahawks may need more muscle in their receiving game, which Goedert may be able to give them in their quest to contend for another Super Bowl.
articles.body:
The Seattle Seahawks may strengthen their chances of defending their Super Bowl title by pursuing a trade for Philadelphia Eagles tight end Dallas Goedert, whose experience and receiving skills figure to give the offense another proven weapon in the receiving game.

Sports Illustrated named Goedert as being one of 15 players most likely to be traded by the deadline this year, and listed the Seahawks as being a fit for him in the trade market.

"Rumors have suggested the Eagles might move off Goedert as he's aged and dealt with injuries, missing at least three games in four of the past five years," Sports Illustrated's Matt Verderame said. "Yet, Goedert has held on, and now might be the time for Philadelphia to cut ties. Goedert is 31 years old and hasn't had 600 yards since the 2022 season. He won't bring a premium, but Goedert is a useful player with a ton of postseason experience."

Goedert has been a productive tight end throughout his NFL career, as he's led with reliable hands, physicality and the ability to gain yards after the catch. His established track record makes him an appealing option for Seattle as it looks to keep its championship window open for years to come. His current season statistics — 17 receptions for 180 receiving yards and two REC touchdowns — provide a clearer picture of his production and potential value in a trade.

Seattle's need for depth is highlighted by AJ Barner's 15 receptions for 138 yards through six games this season, with no touchdowns. Elijah Arroyo being out due to injury further strengthens the case for adding an experienced tight end who is capable of contributing immediately.

Goedert's championship pedigree also makes him an intriguing option. A Super Bowl champion with Philadelphia, he understands what is required to win in the postseason. For Seattle, acquiring a veteran with that experience may give the team a meaningful boost as it pursues back-to-back Super Bowl titles this season. Any potential trade will hinge on the Eagles' willingness to part with Goedert and the Seahawks' assessment of the cost, but his combination of production, experience and postseason success makes him a logical target to pursue.

articles.title: Jordan Elliott Was Released by Titans After Pulling Out Gun in Parking Lot, Coach Robert Saleh Says
articles.summary: Tennessee Titans coach Robert Saleh confirmed Wednesday that defensive tackle Jordan Elliott was released after pulling a gun in the parking lot of the team facility but said it was a "terrible lapse in judgment that I recognize as a call for help more than a criminal act."
articles.body:
Tennessee Titans coach Robert Saleh confirmed Wednesday that defensive tackle Jordan Elliott was released after pulling a gun in the parking lot of the team facility but said it was a "terrible lapse in judgment that I recognize as a call for help more than a criminal act."

The Titans had announced Tuesday that Elliott was released, saying only that it came after his involvement in an unspecified incident at the team's facility five days earlier.

A person briefed on the incident told The Associated Press on Wednesday that Elliott had a gun in his car and went to the parking lot to retrieve it after a dispute with another player. The person spoke to the AP on condition of anonymity because the incident is being reviewed.

Elliott's agent, Malki Kawa, could not be reached for comment.

The NFL prohibits league personnel from taking a firearm to club facilities, stadiums and team hotels and on team planes or buses.

The Titans promptly notified the league of the incident involving Elliott, which is being reviewed, the NFL said.

Speaking to reporters, Saleh defended Jordan's character.

"Unfortunately, rules are rules with regard to guns on property, and sometimes it's far greater than the knee-jerk reaction of kicking somebody when they're down," the coach said.

"He's a good man. Made a terrible, had a terrible lapse in judgment that I recognize as a call for help more than a criminal act," Saleh added. "He's never committed a crime in his entire life and he pulled a gun, in the parking lot."

Right tackle JC Latham, who was involved in the altercation with Elliott on the practice field, called the episode an unfortunate situation.

"I don't really have too much to say about it," Latham said Wednesday. "There ain't never been no bad blood between us two. We were here on the summer getting treatment. Before that, we hung out whenever we were in the same city together. We actually had never had an argument leading up to it."

Elliott appeared in five games this season with one start and had 11 tackles. He followed Saleh to Nashville after a two-year stint with the San Francisco 49ers, where he played in 31 games with 29 starts.

The 6-foot-4 defensive tackle was selected by the Cleveland Browns in the third round of the 2020 draft. He spent his first four seasons in Cleveland before signing a two-year, $7 million deal with San Francisco.

Tennessee added him as a free agent in the offseason on a two-year, $8 million deal.

AP Pro Football Writer Rob Maaddi in Tampa, Florida, contributed to this report.

articles.title: NFL breaks its silence on Troy Aikman and Joe Buck
articles.summary: Joe Buck and Troy Aikman have been one of the most stable broadcast booths in sports for more than two decades, but things have gotten a little awkward betwe...
articles.body:
Joe Buck and Troy Aikman have been one of the most stable broadcast booths in sports for more than two decades, but things have gotten a little awkward between the ESPN duo lately. Aikman's contract situation has hung over the Monday Night Football booth all season, and the two reportedly argued about it before a recent broadcast.

While it might be a massive storyline in the NFL media sphere, the NFL doesn't seem to be worried about it. On Wednesday, league chief media officer Hans Schroeder said that the NFL has "no concern" about the relationship, pointing to the pair's call of Monday night's 49ers-Commanders game as proof.

Last week, Ryan Glasspiegel of Front Office Sports reported that Buck and Aikman argued ahead of ESPN's Oct. 12 Rams-Bills broadcast , after Buck raised the subject of his new contract with Aikman.

ESPN signed Buck to a significant contract extension back in September, but Aikman is in the final year of his deal, and he has not received a formal offer from the network.

Aikman didn't deny the argument, and he has made it clear that he believes ESPN is preparing to move on without him.

"It just seems to be where they're going — that they're gonna go in a different direction because there's been no talks, no contract negotiations," Aikman told Jimmy Traina, via Awful Announcing . "We're in a Super Bowl year. The Super Bowl is Feb. 14. My contract ends in March. It just doesn't seem logical that if they were gonna keep me, something wouldn't be in place before that."

And according to a report from In Touch Weekly, the argument may have been more heated than it first seemed. An anonymous source told the outlet that it "nearly got physical off air," and that the two were "very close from coming to blows."

The source also claimed that Buck "never said a word to Troy" about his new deal, calling it "the biggest betrayal anyone in the industry can remember."

If ESPN does move on, Puck's John Ourand has reported that his sources expect Greg Olsen to replace Aikman .

As the story has grown, the NFL has now officially addressed the incident. When asked about the tension on Wednesday, Schroeder pointed to Monday night's game, in which the 49ers held on for a 23-17 win over the Commanders.

"No concern. I don't know if you watched the game on Monday night. It was an incredible game, right? It was an incredible game and incredible coverage by Joe and Troy, just like they always do," Schroeder said, via Mark Maske of Front Office Sports .

Schroeder also made it clear that the league isn't going to get involved in Aikman's contract situation.

"So, look, that's something… that we're really not involved with," Schroeder said. "I think the fans are deserving of first-class game production, which Joe and Troy have, I think, going back to '02 or something was their first year, a history of doing that as well as anyone."

"And I think you'll continue to see them do that as well as anyone. I thought it was awesome Monday night. And so we're incredibly excited about the year… and the Super Bowl and their coverage," Schroeder added. "They're going to do an unbelievable job."

Buck and Aikman are set to call Super Bowl LXI for ESPN and ABC in February. It's certainly an awkward situation, but it sounds like the NFL is content with things moving forward as planned.

articles.title: Josh Jacobs Apologizes to Teammates as He Gets Ready to Play Again Amid Ongoing NFL Investigation
articles.summary: GREEN BAY, Wis. (AP) — Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs apologized to teammates as he returned to practice Wednesday and talked to reporters for the first time since pleading no contest to two misdemeanor charges stemming from a May altercation with his then-girlfriend during which she said he threw her to the ground.
articles.body:
GREEN BAY, Wis. (AP) — Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs apologized to teammates as he returned to practice Wednesday and talked to reporters for the first time since pleading no contest to two misdemeanor charges stemming from a May altercation with his then-girlfriend during which she said he threw her to the ground.

"Obviously, man, I'm remorseful and sorry for putting this team in this situation," Jacobs said. "Sometimes when you go through life, situations occur and a four-second, three-second decision can alter your life, honestly."

Jacobs was removed this week from the commissioner's exempt list , which had prevented him from playing or practicing. The NFL had placed Jacobs on that list Aug. 30, shortly after charges were filed against him. He pleaded no contest last month to misdemeanor counts of battery and criminal damage to property.

The NFL is still investigating Jacobs over the incident, so the league still could hand out more discipline to the three-time Pro Bowl running back. But for now, Jacobs is eligible to play again for the Packers after missing the first six games of the season.

"I thought I'd be playing sooner," Jacobs said. "But, you know, the optics of everything, I understand the other side. For me, like I said, I'm just grateful to be able to play. It was one of them things where I didn't want to sit the whole year and then figure it out. I'm just grateful to be back on the team and to be back playing."

Jacobs doesn't discuss details of his arrest

Jacobs was arrested May 26, three days after police officers came to his Wisconsin home to investigate a disturbance. According to police, the woman told them that Jacobs grabbed her and threw her to the ground as she was trying to exit a garage door, causing her to hit her head. Police said Jacobs also took her phone from her while she was on the ground.

Police said they noticed redness on her face and neck and could feel a bump on the back of her head.

The criminal complaint against him noted that a surveillance video from the camera system in their garage corroborated the woman's statement. Both Jacobs and the victim have gone to court attempting to have that video and other evidence sealed permanently.

Jacobs declined to discuss the specifics of his case but said he hopes to use the situation as an opportunity to grow into a better person.

"Obviously you never want to be in this situation, but just me being honest, for my life, it was probably one of the best things to ever happen to me," Jacobs said. "I say that because it gave me a chance to sit down and reevaluate what's important and what I want my life to look like, and what do I want people to know me for. When they think of me, what are they going to say?"

Jacobs didn't fear possibility he might not play again

Jacobs was asked Wednesday if he'd feared the possibility he might never play again after his arrest.

"I wasn't overly concerned about that because in my heart, I know what happened and what didn't happen," Jacobs said. "And I'll just trust the legal process. So for me, I wasn't ever overly concerned of not playing again. It was just a matter of when."

Green Bay quarterback Jordan Love said Jacobs had spoken to the team and that the Packers are "happy to have Josh back, for sure." Green Bay's offense ranks last in the NFL in yards rushing per game (59.8) and yards per carry (2.9).

Coach Matt LaFleur hasn't indicated what kind of workload Jacobs might get Sunday at Detroit, or even whether he would play at all. Jacobs was unable to practice or play while on the commissioner's exempt list, but he was able to attend meetings and lift weights and condition with the Packers' strength coaches.

"I think people learn from their mistakes and I think he's extremely remorseful and I do believe that he's a good person," LaFleur said. "I've been around him quite a bit and I just, I believe in second chances."

LaFleur's comment Wednesday was more measured than what he said Sept. 1, after the charges were filed but before Jacobs pleaded no contest to the two misdemeanors. LaFleur said then that "I believe him and I trust him" and added that "I'm going to do that until proven otherwise."

Jacobs was asked if he feels he needs to earn back the respect of teammates and what he would say to fans.

"I don't think I had to earn respect back from the guys because I'm the same person every day," Jacobs said. "Like I said, at the end of the day, we're human. We all make mistakes. It's just different for me because I'm in the public eye. But you know, like I said, I'll let other people speak to my character and who I am and who I consistently have been.

"When it comes to earning the respect of the fans, I mean, for me, it's more of a thing of not trying to put this organization in a position where it looks negative in any type of way. But at the end of the day, people are always going to have their opinion. People are going to believe what they believe, and it's not really my job to try to explain or discount certain things. All I can try to do is control what I can control and move on from there."
